summary: This article explains how the fennec fox and other desert foxes use big ears, furry paws, sandy coats, burrows, and night hunting to survive in hot, dry deserts.
introduce: Show the title “Desert Foxes: Big Ears, Small Bodies” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a body part or way of acting that helps a living thing survive where it lives
colors or patterns that help an animal blend in so it is hard to see
an animal that hunts and eats other animals

challengeTerms.def: to spread out and disappear, or to make something such as heat do this
to keep something from being lost or wasted

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a small animal can survive in the desert better than a big one? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Choose the fennec fox adaptation you think is most important.
struggling: Pre-teach adaptation, camouflage, and predator with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use dissipate, acute, and conserve in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
